abstract: Deloitte's State of AI in the Enterprise 2026 report, based on a survey of 3,235 senior leaders across 24 countries conducted August-September 2025, documents the maturation of enterprise AI adoption. Worker access to AI increased by 50% in 2025, and 71% of organizations regularly use generative AI in at least one business function (up from 65% in early 2024). The number of companies with 40%+ of AI projects in production is expected to double within six months. On impact, 66% report productivity and efficiency gains, 53% enhanced decision-making, and 40% cost reductions, though only 20% report increased revenue despite 74% aspiring to it — highlighting a gap between productivity optimization and revenue transformation. The workforce dimension reveals that insufficient worker skills is the biggest integration barrier, with 53% of organizations educating their workforce for AI fluency and 48% implementing upskilling programs. Only 30% are reimagining organizational structures. A governance gap exists: 42% believe their strategy is highly prepared for AI, but fewer feel operationally ready on infrastructure, data, risk management, and talent. For agentic AI specifically, only 20% have mature governance models. Physical AI adoption stands at 58% currently, projected to reach 80% within two years.
keyFindings: 71% of organizations regularly use generative AI in at least one business function, up from 65% in early 2024, with worker access increasing 50% in 2025.
66% report productivity gains but only 20% report increased revenue, revealing a gap between efficiency optimization and top-line transformation.
Insufficient worker skills is the biggest AI integration barrier; 53% are educating workforces for fluency, 48% running upskilling programs, but only 30% reimagining org structures.
Only 20% of companies have mature governance models for agentic AI, despite 58% already using physical AI in some capacity.
34% of organizations are deeply transforming business through AI (new products, reimagined processes), while 37% remain at surface-level integration.
methodology: Survey of 3,235 senior leaders (C-suite executives and board members) conducted August-September 2025 across 24 countries. Equal representation between IT and business leadership. Published as part of Deloitte's ongoing State of AI in the Enterprise research series, which has tracked enterprise AI adoption annually.
qualifiers: The sample of 3,235 senior leaders skews toward large enterprises with dedicated AI strategies, likely overstating adoption rates relative to the broader economy. Self-reported productivity gains (66%) may reflect optimism bias rather than measured outcomes. The survey was conducted August-September 2025, and the pace of AI evolution means findings may not reflect current conditions. Deloitte is a major AI consulting services provider with commercial interest in framing AI adoption as accelerating. The 'regularly use' threshold is not precisely defined and may include superficial adoption.
